books.title: Stablecoins
books.blurb: Follow Ana's $100 as it becomes a digital dollar: what backs it, who earns the interest, the rules around the world, and what it means for you.
gist: A stablecoin is a digital claim ticket worth $1, backed mostly by short US government IOUs and cash.
The interest on that backing goes to the issuer and its partners; holders get none, by law in the US and EU.
It is fast and works 24/7, but it is not a bank account: no deposit insurance, and it can wobble below $1.

books.title: Why is everything so expensive?
books.blurb: Why prices keep climbing, told through Sam's $100 Saturday shop.
gist: Inflation means the same money buys less: US prices roughly doubled from 2000 to 2026.
The 2021-22 spike had several causes stacked together: money and demand, supply chains, energy and some company pricing.
Inflation quietly moves buying power between shoppers, savers, workers, borrowers and governments.
